newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices extend gains, soften late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices extend gains, soften late.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were mostly higher again Wednesday, still boosted by swing demand after a lightly-traded bidweek and storage demand in the U.S. producing region, market sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices rose another five cents to an average range of $1.87-1.92 per mmBtu, though deals were reported done as high as $1.97 and as low as $1.84.
"The market rallied early, then went lower, but then came back a little late," one Houston-based trader said.
At the Henry Hub, gas traded early in the mid-$1.90s, but prices then eroded into the mid-$1.80s.
In the East, swing prices in the Appalachian region climbed above $2 early but traded in the mid-$1.90s in late morning trade.
At the New York city-gate, prices soared to as high as $2.30 but then settled into the teens late, compared with Tuesday's $2.08-2.13 trading range.
In the Midcontinent, prices rose by about 10 cents to the low-$1.80s, with Chicago city-gate values quoted in the $2.00-2.10 range.
In the Permian basin, gas prices were also up about 10 cents to an average range of $1.81-1.86.
At Waha, prices were talked in the $1.83-1.90 range, with the lower-priced deals evident in late trading. Southern California border prices ranged anywhere from $1.84 to $1.96.
"West Coast buyers are definitely out there buying, and power prices are up," one trader said, noting the increase in demand was tightening the market.
The 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California is still scheduled to restart around March 12 following repairs of a leak, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said.
Withdrawal estimates for today's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from 60 to 105 bcf, with most at 70-80 bcf, according to a Reuter poll.
